title: Containers and VMs: when to use each

videos.script: Containers come up in every conversation about virtual machines, usually as if they were a lighter kind of virtual machine. They are something else, and the difference decides which one a job needs. {{else}} A virtual machine is a whole computer, with its own kernel, made of software. A container is a group of ordinary processes on the host, with a restricted view of it. {{what}} You will run both side by side, and ask each the same questions. Which kernel are you running? How long did you take to start? And what does the host see of you? {{questions}} The answers make the choice simple. And the computer this course was recorded on turns out to be an example of both at once. {{both}}
